sanskrit: kharaṃ tu virathaṃ rāmo gadāpāṇim avasthitam mṛdupūrvaṃ mahātejāḥ paruṣaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, of great radiance, first gently and then harshly addressed Khara, who stood dismounted from his chariot, mace in hand.

sanskrit: gajāśvarathasaṃbādhe bale mahati tiṣṭhatā kṛtaṃ sudāruṇaṃ karma sarvalokajugupsitam
english: Standing amid a great force of elephants, horses, and chariots, you have performed a most terrible deed that all the worlds condemn.

sanskrit: udvejanīyo bhūtānāṃ nṛśaṃsaḥ pāpakarmakṛt trayāṇām api lokānām īśvaro 'pi na tiṣṭhati
english: One who is cruel, a doer of evil deeds, and a cause of terror to all beings cannot endure even if he be lord of the three worlds.

sanskrit: karma lokaviruddhaṃ tu kurvāṇaṃ kṣaṇadācara tīkṣṇaṃ sarvajano hanti sarpaṃ duṣṭam ivāgatam
english: One who acts against the world's order, O night-roaming demon, all people destroy sharply, as one destroys a venomous snake that approaches.

sanskrit: lobhāt pāpāni kurvāṇaḥ kāmād vā yo na budhyate bhraṣṭaḥ paśyati tasyāntaṃ brāhmaṇī karakād iva
english: He who, out of greed or passion, commits sins and does not understand, ruined, he sees his own end — as a Brahmin woman watches a hailstone melt away.

sanskrit: vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tāpasān dharmacāriṇaḥ kiṃ nu hatvā mahābhāgān phalaṃ prāpsyasi rākṣasa
english: What fruit do you think you will obtain, O demon, by slaying the noble ascetics, those who walk in righteousness, dwelling here in the Daṇḍaka forest?

sanskrit: na ciraṃ pāpakarmāṇaḥ krūrā lokajugupsitāḥ aiśvaryaṃ prāpya tiṣṭhanti śīrṇamūlā iva drumāḥ
english: Those who do evil deeds, the cruel and those condemned by the world, do not long retain their lordship once gained — like trees whose roots have rotted.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ labhate kartā phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ ghoraṃ paryāgate kāle drumaḥ puṣpam ivārtavam
english: The doer inevitably reaps the terrible fruit of evil action when the time comes around, as a tree blooms in its season.

sanskrit: nacirāt prāpyate loke pāpānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalam saviṣāṇām ivānnānāṃ bhuktānāṃ kṣaṇadācara
english: The fruit of evil actions is swiftly obtained in this world, O night-wandering demon, like food laced with poison once it has been eaten.

sanskrit: pāpam āccaratāṃ ghoraṃ lokasyāpriyam icchatām aham āsādito rājā prāṇān hantuṃ niśācara
english: I am a king appointed to slay those who commit terrible sin and who seek what is harmful to the world — I have come to take your life, O night-prowler.

sanskrit: adya hi tvāṃ mayā muktāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ vidārya nipatiṣyanti valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Today the gold-adorned arrows I release will tear through you and fall upon you as serpents descend upon an anthill.

sanskrit: ye tvayā daṇḍakāraṇye bhakṣitā dharmacāriṇaḥ tān adya nihataḥ saṃkhye sasainyo 'nugamiṣyasi
english: Those righteous ones whom you devoured in the Daṇḍaka forest — today, slain in battle along with your army, you shall follow them.

sanskrit: adya tvāṃ nihataṃ bāṇaiḥ paśyantu paramarṣayaḥ nirayasthaṃ vimānasthā ye tvayā hiṃsitāḥ purā
english: May the great sages whom you once harmed, now seated in their celestial cars, look down today and behold you laid low by arrows, fallen into hell.

sanskrit: prahara tvaṃ yathākāmaṃ kuru yatnaṃ kulādhama adya te pātayiṣyāmi śiras tālaphalaṃ yathā
english: Strike as you wish, make your utmost effort, O disgrace to your lineage — today I shall strike off your head as one strikes down a palm fruit.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa kruddhaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ pratyuvāca tato rāmaṃ prahasan krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Khara, enraged with blood-red eyes, laughed and replied to Rāma, overcome with fury.

sanskrit: prākṛtān rākṣasān hatvā yuddhe daśarathātmaja ātmanā katham ātmānam apraśasyaṃ praśaṃsasi
english: Having slain mere common rākṣasas in battle, O son of Daśaratha, how do you praise yourself — though self-praise is ignoble?

sanskrit: vikrāntā balavanto vā ye bhavanti nararṣabhāḥ kathayanti na te kiṃ cit tejasā svena garvitāḥ
english: Truly valiant and mighty men, the bulls among men, say nothing of themselves, even when filled with their own blazing splendour.

sanskrit: prākṛtās tv akṛtātmāno loke kṣatriyapāṃsanāḥ nirarthakaṃ vikatthante yathā rāma vikatthase
english: Only the ignoble, the undisciplined, the stains upon the Kṣatriya order in this world boast uselessly, as you, O Rāma, boast.

sanskrit: kulaṃ vyapadiśan vīraḥ samare ko 'bhidhāsyati mṛtyukāle hi saṃprāpte svayam aprastave stavam
english: What hero in battle would invoke his lineage and sing his own praises unprompted, when the hour of death has arrived?

sanskrit: sarvathā tu laghutvaṃ te katthanena vidarśitam suvarṇapratirūpeṇa tapteneva kuśāgninā
english: In every way your smallness has been revealed by your boasting, like fool's gold revealed by the fire of a touchstone.

sanskrit: na tu mām iha tiṣṭhantaṃ paśyasi tvaṃ gadādharam dharādharam ivākampyaṃ parvataṃ dhātubhiś citam
english: Do you not see me standing here, mace in hand, immovable as a mountain bearing the earth, streaked with its veins of ore?

sanskrit: paryāpto 'haṃ gadāpāṇir hantuṃ prāṇān raṇe tava trayāṇām api lokānāṃ pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ
english: I am fully capable, mace in hand, of taking your life in battle — even as Yama with noose in hand rules the three worlds.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ bahv api vaktavyaṃ tvayi vakṣyāmi na tv aham astaṃ gacched dhi savitā yuddhavighras tato bhavet
english: There is much indeed I could say to you, yet I will not — for should the sun set, battle would thereby be hindered.

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rākṣasānāṃ hatāni te tvadvināśāt karomy adya teṣām aśrupramārjanam
english: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas have been slain — by destroying you today I shall wipe away their tears.

sanskrit: ity uktvā paramakruddhas tāṃ gadāṃ paramāṅgadām kharaś cikṣepa rāmāya pradīptām aśaniṃ yathā
english: Having spoken thus, in supreme fury Khara hurled that great mace, blazing like a thunderbolt, at Rāma.

sanskrit: kharabāhupramuktā sā pradīptā mahatī gadā bhasmavṛkṣāṃś ca gulmāṃś ca kṛtvāgāt tatsamīpataḥ
english: That great blazing mace, released from Khara's arm, reduced trees and shrubs to ash as it flew toward Rāma.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ jvalitāṃ mṛtyupāśopamāṃ gadā antarikṣagatāṃ rāmaś ciccheda bahudhā śaraiḥ
english: As that blazing mace, like death's own noose, flew through the air toward him, Rāma shattered it into many pieces with his arrows.

sanskrit: sā viśīrṇā śarair bhinnā papāta dharaṇītale gadāmantrauṣadhibalair vyālīva vinipātitā
english: Shattered and pierced by those arrows, it fell to the ground, like a great serpent brought down by the power of mantras and herbs.

sanskrit: bhittvā tu tāṃ gadāṃ bāṇai rāghavo dharmavatsalaḥ smayamānaḥ kharaṃ vākyaṃ saṃrabdham idam abravīt
english: Having split that mace with his arrows, Rāghava, devoted to righteousness, smiled and spoke these fierce words to Khara.

sanskrit: etat te balasarvasvaṃ darśitaṃ rākṣasādhama śaktihīnataro matto vṛthā tvam upagarjitam
english: You have shown the full extent of your strength, O vilest of rākṣasas — you are more feeble than I, and your roaring was in vain.

sanskrit: eṣā bāṇavinirbhinnā gadā bhūmitalaṃ gatā abhidhānapragalbhasya tava pratyayaghātinī
english: This mace, pierced by my arrows, has gone to the ground — a refutation of your arrogant boasting.

sanskrit: yat tvayoktaṃ vinaṣṭānām idam aśrupramārjanam rākṣasānāṃ karomīti mithyā tad api te vacaḥ
english: As for what you said — "I shall wipe away the tears of the slain rākṣasas" — that too was a false boast.

sanskrit: nīcasya kṣudraśīlasya mithyāvṛttasya rakṣasaḥ prāṇān apahariṣyāmi garutmān amṛtaṃ yathā
english: From this base, mean-natured, false-living demon I shall take his life as Garuḍa seizes the amṛta.

sanskrit: adya te bhinnakaṇṭhasya phenabudbudabhūṣitam vidāritasya madbāṇair mahī pāsyati śoṇitam
english: Today the earth shall drink your blood, foaming and bubbling, as my arrows split open your throat and rend your body.

sanskrit: pāṃsurūṣitasarvāṅgaḥ srastanyastabhujadvayaḥ svapsyase gāṃ samāśliṣya durlabhāṃ pramadām iva
english: With every limb smeared in dust, your two arms fallen and outstretched, you shall sleep embracing the earth as if she were a rare and beloved woman.

sanskrit: pravṛddhanidre śayite tvayi rākṣasapāṃsane bhaviṣyanty aśaraṇyānāṃ śaraṇyā daṇḍakā ime
english: When you lie sunk in the deepest sleep, O disgrace of the rākṣasas, these Daṇḍaka forests shall become a refuge for those who now have no refuge.

sanskrit: janasthāne hatasthāne tava rākṣasamaccharaiḥ nirbhayā vicariṣyanti sarvato munayo vane
english: With Janasthāna become a place of slaughter for your rākṣasas by my arrows, the sages shall roam fearlessly in every part of the forest.

sanskrit: adya viprasariṣyanti rākṣasyo hatabāndhavāḥ bāṣpārdravadanā dīnā bhayād anyabhayāvahāḥ
english: Today the rākṣasī women, their kinsmen slain, faces drenched with tears, wretched and themselves a terror to others, shall scatter in flight.

sanskrit: adya śokarasajñās tā bhaviṣyanti niśācara anurūpakulāḥ patnyo yāsāṃ tvaṃ patir īdṛśaḥ
english: Today, O night-prowler, those wives who belong to a lineage fitted for such a lord as you shall come to taste the full flavour of grief.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaśīla kṣudrātman nityaṃ brāhmaṇakaṇṭaka tvatkṛte śaṅkitair agnau munibhiḥ pātyate haviḥ
english: O cruel-natured one, petty of soul, ever a thorn to Brāhmaṇas — because of you the sages cast their oblations into the fire with trembling hands.

sanskrit: tam evam abhisaṃrabdhaṃ bruvāṇaṃ rāghavaṃ raṇe kharo nirbhartsayām āsa roṣāt kharatara svanaḥ
english: As Rāghava spoke thus in fierce passion in battle, Khara, his voice even harsher in rage, reviled him harshly.

sanskrit: dṛḍhaṃ khalv avalipto 'si bhayeṣv api ca nirbhayaḥ vācyāvācyaṃ tato hi tvaṃ mṛtyuvaśyo na budhyase
english: You are thoroughly puffed up with pride and fearless even in the face of peril — that is why you do not discern what should and should not be said, for you are already in the grip of death.

sanskrit: kālapāśaparikṣiptā bhavanti puruṣā hi ye kāryākāryaṃ na jānanti te nirastaṣaḍindriyāḥ
english: Those men who are ensnared in the noose of Death know not what should or should not be done — their six senses are utterly swept away.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rāmaṃ saṃrudhya bhṛkuṭiṃ tataḥ sa dadarśa mahāsālam avidūre niśācaraḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Rāma, furrowing his brow in fury, the night-roaming demon then caught sight of a great śāla tree nearby.

sanskrit: raṇe praharaṇasyārthe sarvato hy avalokayan sa tam utpāṭayām āsa saṃdṛśya daśanacchadam
english: Looking all around for a weapon to use in battle, he fixed his gaze upon that tree and baring his teeth uprooted it.

sanskrit: taṃ samutkṣipya bāhubhyāṃ vinarditvā mahābalaḥ rāmam uddiśya cikṣepa hatas tvam iti cābravīt
english: Lifting it aloft with both arms and roaring mightily, that one of great power hurled it at Rāma, crying out: "You are slain!"

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ bāṇaughaiś chittvā rāmaḥ pratāpavān roṣam āhārayat tīvraṃ nihantuṃ samare kharam
english: Rāma, of blazing valour, cut down that oncoming tree with a shower of arrows, then drew up fierce fury within himself to slay Khara in battle.

sanskrit: jātasvedas tato rāmo roṣād raktāntalocanaḥ nirbibheda sahasreṇa bāṇānāṃ samare kharam
english: Then Rāma, perspiring, his eyes red at their corners with rage, pierced Khara in battle with a thousand arrows.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇāntarād raktaṃ bahu susrāva phenilam gireḥ prasravaṇasyeva toyadhārāparisravaḥ
english: From the gaps between the arrows blood flowed forth in great foaming streams, like the rushing flow of water cascading from a mountain spring.

sanskrit: vihvalaḥ sa kṛto bāṇaiḥ kharo rāmeṇa saṃyuge matto rudhiragandhena tam evābhyadravad drutam
english: Though made frantic by the arrows in combat with Rāma, Khara, intoxicated by the smell of blood, rushed swiftly at him.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ kṛtāstro rudhirāplutam apasarpat pratipadaṃ kiṃ cit tvaritavikramaḥ
english: As he charged in frenzied fury, drenched in blood, Rāma — skilled in weaponry — with swift, measured steps yielded ground slightly before him.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāvakasaṃkāśaṃ badhāya samare śaram kharasya rāmo jagrāha brahmadaṇḍam ivāparam
english: Then Rāma took up an arrow blazing like fire for the killing of Khara in battle — a second rod of Brahmā, as it were.

sanskrit: sa tad dattaṃ maghavatā surarājena dhīmatā saṃdadhe ca sa dharmātmā mumoca ca kharaṃ prati
english: That arrow — given formerly by the wise king of the gods, Maghavat (Indra) — the righteous-souled Rāma nocked and released it toward Khara.

sanskrit: sa vimukto mahābāṇo nirghātasamaniḥsvanaḥ rāmeṇa dhanur udyamya kharasyorasi cāpatat
english: Released with the bow raised, that mighty arrow, thundering like a thunderclap, struck Khara square in the chest.

sanskrit: sa papāta kharo bhūmau dahyamānaḥ śarāgninā rudreṇaiva vinirdagdhaḥ śvetāraṇye yathāndhakaḥ
english: Khara fell to the ground, consumed by the fire of that arrow, even as Andhaka was burned up by Rudra himself in the Śveta forest.

sanskrit: sa vṛtra iva vajreṇa phenena namucir yathā balo vendrāśanihato nipapāta hataḥ kharaḥ
english: Khara fell slain — as Vṛtra fell by the thunderbolt, as Namuci fell by the foam, as Bali fell struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato rājarṣayaḥ sarve saṃgatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ sabhājya muditā rāmam idaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: Then all the royal sages and the great seers assembled together, honoured Rāma with joyful hearts, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ mahātejā mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ śarabhaṅgāśramaṃ puṇyam ājagāma puraṃdaraḥ
english: For this very purpose did the great and resplendent Mahendra, the chastiser of Pāka, the destroyer of cities, come to the sacred hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.

sanskrit: ānītas tvam imaṃ deśam upāyena maharṣibhiḥ eṣāṃ vadhārthaṃ krūrāṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ pāpakarmaṇām
english: You were brought to this region by the device of the great sages, for the purpose of slaying these cruel rākṣasas of evil deeds.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ tvayā daśarathātmaja sukhaṃ dharmaṃ cariṣyanti daṇḍakeṣu maharṣayaḥ
english: This task of ours has been accomplished by you, O son of Daśaratha — the great sages shall now live and follow righteousness in the Daṇḍaka forests in peace.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīro lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā giridurgād viniṣkramya saṃviveśāśramaṃ sukhī
english: In the meantime, the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, together with Sītā, emerged from the mountain fortress and happily entered their hermitage.

sanskrit: tato rāmas tu vijayī pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ praviveśāśramaṃ vīro lakṣmaṇenābhivāditaḥ
english: Then the victorious hero Rāma, honoured by the great sages, entered the hermitage, greeted with reverence by Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā śatruhantāraṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sukhāvaham babhūva hṛṣṭā vaidehī bhartāraṃ pariṣasvaje
english: Seeing him — the destroyer of enemies, the bringer of joy to the great sages — Vaidehī was filled with delight and embraced her husband.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā dṛṣṭvā sahasrāṇi caturdaśa hatāny ekena rāmeṇa rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām
english: Then Śūrpaṇakhā, having seen fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds slain single-handedly by Rāma,

sanskrit: dūṣaṇaṃ ca kharaṃ caiva hataṃ triśirasaṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā punar mahānādaṃ nanāda jaladopamā
english: and Dūṣaṇa, Khara, and Triśiras slain in battle, let out once more a great cry, like a cloud bursting.

sanskrit: sā dṛṣṭvā karma rāmasya kṛtam anyaiḥ suduṣkaram jagāma paramaudvignā laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām
english: Having witnessed this deed of Rāma's, impossible for others to accomplish, she went in extreme agitation to Laṅkā, the realm protected by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa vimānāgre rāvaṇaṃ dīptatejasaṃ upopaviṣṭaṃ sacivair marudbhir iva vāsavam
english: She saw Rāvaṇa at the fore of his palace, blazing with splendour, seated in the company of his ministers as Vāsava sits surrounded by the Maruts.

sanskrit: āsīnaṃ sūryasaṃkāśe kāñcane paramāsane rukmavedigataṃ prājyaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam
english: Seated upon a splendid golden throne brilliant as the sun, placed upon a golden dais, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: devagandharvabhūtānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām ajeyaṃ samare śūraṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam
english: Unconquerable in battle by gods, gandharvas, spirits, and great-souled sages alike — a hero with gaping mouth like Death himself.

sanskrit: devāsuravimardeṣu vajrāśanikṛtavraṇam airāvataviṣāṇāgrair utkṛṣṭakiṇavakṣasaṃ
english: His body bearing scars made by Indra's thunderbolt in battles between gods and asuras, his chest scarred and furrowed by the tusks of Airāvata.

sanskrit: viṃśadbhujaṃ daśagrīvaṃ darśanīyaparicchadam viśālavakṣasaṃ vīraṃ rājalakṣmaṇalakṣitam
english: Twenty-armed, ten-headed, with splendid attire, broad-chested, heroic, bearing the marks of royalty.

sanskrit: snigdhavaidūryasaṃkāśaṃ taptakāñcanakuṇḍalam subhujaṃ śukladaśanaṃ mahāsyaṃ parvatopamam
english: His complexion like polished vaidūrya gem, wearing earrings of burnished gold, with handsome arms, white teeth, a vast mouth, and a form like a mountain.

sanskrit: viṣṇucakranipātaiś ca śataśo devasaṃyuge āhatāṅgaṃ samastaiś ca devapraharaṇais tathā
english: His body struck hundreds of times by Viṣṇu's discus in battles with the gods, and likewise by all the weapons of the devas.

sanskrit: akṣobhyāṇāṃ samudrāṇāṃ kṣobhaṇaṃ kṣiprakāriṇam kṣeptāraṃ parvatāgrāṇāṃ surāṇāṃ ca pramardanam
english: Who stirs the unstirrable oceans, swift in action, who hurls the peaks of mountains and crushes the gods.

sanskrit: ucchettāraṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ paradārābhimarśanam sarvadivyāstrayoktāraṃ yajñavighnakaraṃ sadā
english: Destroyer of righteousness, violator of others' wives, wielder of all divine weapons, ever a disrupter of sacrifices.

sanskrit: purīṃ bhogavatīṃ gatvā parājitya ca vāsukim takṣakasya priyāṃ bhāryāṃ parājitya jahāra yaḥ
english: Who went to the city of Bhogavatī, defeated Vāsuki, and then overpowering Takṣaka, carried off his beloved wife.

sanskrit: kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gatvā vijitya naravāhanam vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ tasya kāmagaṃ vai jahāra yaḥ
english: Who went to Mount Kailāsa, defeated Kubera who rides men as his vehicle, and seized his wish-fulfilling aerial chariot, the Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: vanaṃ caitrarathaṃ divyaṃ nalinīṃ nandanaṃ vanam vināśayati yaḥ krodhād devodyānāni vīryavān
english: Who, mighty in valour, out of rage devastates the celestial garden of Caitraratha, and the lotus pond, and the grove of Nandana, and the parks of the gods.

sanskrit: candrasūryau mahābhāgāv uttiṣṭhantau paraṃtapau nivārayati bāhubhyāṃ yaḥ śailaśikharopamaḥ
english: Who, standing like a mountain peak, holds back with his own arms the mighty Sun and Moon when they rise — those two of great splendour who afflict their foes.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tapas taptvā mahāvane purā svayambhuve dhīraḥ śirāṃsy upajahāra yaḥ
english: Who, resolute, in ancient times performed asceticism for ten thousand years in the great forest, and then offered his own heads to Svayambhū (Brahmā).

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvapiśācapatagoragaiḥ abhayaṃ yasya saṃgrāme mṛtyuto mānuṣād ṛte
english: Whom gods, dānavas, gandharvas, piśācas, birds, and serpents cannot threaten with death in battle — save only a mortal man.

sanskrit: mantrar abhituṣṭaṃ puṇyam adhvareṣu dvijātibhiḥ havirdhāneṣu yaḥ somam upahanti mahābalaḥ
english: He of great might who seizes the soma from the sacrificial vessels — the holy and gratifying offerings — when the twice-born perform their sacred rites.

sanskrit: āptayajñaharaṃ krūraṃ brahmaghnaṃ duṣṭacāriṇam karkaśaṃ niranukrośaṃ prajānām ahite ratam rāvaṇaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvalokabhayāvaham
english: That pillager of duly performed sacrifices, cruel, slayer of Brāhmaṇas, of corrupt conduct, harsh, without compassion, intent on harming subjects — Rāvaṇa, a terror to all beings and to all the worlds.

sanskrit: rākṣasī bhrātaraṃ krūraṃ sā dadarśa mahābalam taṃ divyavastrābharaṇaṃ divyamālyopaśobhitam rākṣasendraṃ mahābhāgaṃ paulastya kulanandanam
english: The rākṣasī saw her cruel and mighty brother — adorned with divine garments and ornaments, beautified with divine garlands — the lord of the rākṣasas, the illustrious delight of the Paulastya lineage.

sanskrit: tam abravīd dīptaviśālalocanaṃ pradarśayitvā bhayamohamūrchitā sudāruṇaṃ vākyam abhītacāriṇī mahātmanā śūrpaṇakhā virūpitā
english: Displaying her blazing, wide eyes, overcome with fear, confusion, and anguish, Śūrpaṇakhā — who had walked fearlessly before but was now disfigured by the great-souled Rāma — spoke these most terrible words to him.
